text: Impenetrable means impossible to get through or to understand. Here it describes AI systems so complex that no human mind could follow their reasoning.
To fetishise something is to worship it far more than it deserves. The writer says scientists should not prize understanding so highly that they reject useful results.
Giddying means dizzying and thrilling at once. The prospect of AI mastering biology is both exciting and frightening.
To baffle is to confuse completely. The 372 problems had puzzled scholars for decades.
A discipline is a field of study, such as mathematics or biology. It can also mean self-control, but here it means a branch of knowledge.
Disciplines are fields of study. Scholars will need to rethink how their fields work once AI does much of the proving.
To digest an idea is to take it in and fully understand it, like food. Mathematicians are still working out what the results mean.
To grapple with a problem is to struggle hard to deal with it. The article says it is time to grapple with AI's effect on science.
An axiom is a basic statement in mathematics accepted as true without proof. All proofs are built by logic from axioms.
Empirical means based on observation and experiment rather than pure logic. Biology and physics are empirical sciences; maths is not.
Proteins are large molecules that do most of the work in living cells. Their shape decides what they do, so predicting shapes is very valuable.
Amino acids are the small building blocks that link up in chains to form proteins. AI can predict a protein's shape from its chain.
The Nobel prize is the most famous award in science. The protein-shape advance mentioned here won one.
Nuclear fusion is the process that powers the sun, where light atoms merge and release energy. Scientists hope to harness it for clean power.
In silico is Latin-style slang for done inside a computer, since chips are made of silicon. It contrasts with in vivo, in a living thing.
In an AI model, tokens are the small pieces of text, such as words or word parts, that it reads and writes. The article imagines DNA treated like such a string.
DNA is the molecule that carries the instructions for building living things, written in a four-letter code. The article compares it to computer code.
Drought-resistant crops can survive with little water. AI is being used to design them.
An organism is any living thing, from a bacterium to a whale. Scientists might one day design new ones from scratch.
Terrifying means causing great fear. The writer says AI's prospects are both exciting and terrifying.
To be up in arms is to be angrily protesting. Mathematicians are furious at the lab's entry into their field.
Encroachment is gradually moving into someone else's territory. Mathematicians see the AI lab as intruding on their discipline.
Special pleading means arguing that the normal rules should not apply to your own case. The writer says academics have no special right to control knowledge.
A pay-off is the reward you get for effort. Mathematicians say theirs comes from the toil of doing the work, not just the answer.
Toil is long, hard work. The mathematicians argue the toil is how human understanding grows.
To churn out something is to produce a lot of it quickly, often without much care. Here AIs churn out proofs.
A guild was a medieval association of craftspeople protecting their trade. The writer says scholars should not be a guild controlling truth-seeking.
Sacred means so special it must not be questioned or changed. The writer says academic hierarchies are not sacred.
A hierarchy is a ranking from top to bottom. Academic hierarchies are climbed by proving things.
Remade means rebuilt in a new form. Academic status systems must be rebuilt for a world where AI makes the proofs.
Paracetamol is a common painkiller, called acetaminophen in the United States. Its exact workings were long unclear, yet it helps.
A mechanism is how something works inside. A drug can work without scientists fully knowing its mechanism.
Idle here means pointless or without good reason. The fear of handing science to machines is not idle, meaning it is a serious worry.
Altruism is acting to help others without expecting a reward. The article says AI firms invest in science for their own benefit.
Ploughing resources into something means investing large amounts. It comes from a farmer ploughing a field.
To compete is to try to win against rivals. If AI labs control the best science models, nobody else can.
This phrase signals that a claim is true only if you define the word a certain way. Here it hedges how 'incomprehensibly intelligent' AI would be.
Humanoid robots are machines shaped roughly like people, with arms, legs and a head. They could carry out experiments in the real world.
Hooking up means connecting one thing to another. Models can be connected to lab equipment so they can run experiments.
Anthropic is an American AI company that makes the Claude models. The article notes it has already linked models to lab equipment.
OpenAI is the American AI lab behind ChatGPT. It released the hundreds of maths papers at the center of the story.
A frontier lab is a company building the most advanced AI systems. The term suggests it works at the edge of what is possible.
Writing the cheques means paying for something. If nobody understands what AI does, funding it blindly would be reckless.
Reckless means taking risks without thinking about the consequences. Funding AI nobody understands would be reckless.
To align an AI is to make its goals match human values. Alignment is considered unsolved, so trusting AI fully is premature.
Here pets are animals kept and looked after by their owners. The writer warns that humans relying wholly on AI could become the machines' pets.
Having a human in the loop means a person stays involved to check and approve decisions. The writer says science needs one.
Unshakeable means impossible to doubt or weaken. Alignment would need to be certain before we hand over control.
An informed judgment is a decision based on knowing the facts. Only people who understand what AIs do can make one.
A citizen is a member of a community. Good scientific citizens follow the community's rules, such as peer review.
Peer review is when other experts check a study before publication. The article urges AI labs to submit to it.
Scepticism is a habit of doubting claims until there is good evidence. It is the heart of good science.
Verification means checking that something is true. The article says science needs more of it as AI makes results.
The Royal Society is a famous British scientific academy founded in the 1660s. Its motto urges taking nobody's word for it.
Nullius in verba is Latin for 'take nobody's word for it'. It means claims must be checked against evidence.
From the saying 'don't throw the baby out with the bathwater', meaning do not lose something valuable while discarding the bad. Here the valuable part is human understanding.
